newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Jan 14 - Our final estimate on CPO production in December remained unchanged at 630,000 tonnes. This represents a rather sharp seasonal decline of around 17 percent or 130,000 tonnes. Production in Peninsular Malaysia fell around 18 percent. The performance of major producers/millers ranged from down 10-23 percent. In East Malaysia the range was even wider - from about unchange to down 25 percent. We are also maintaining our end-December palm oil stocks estimate of 805,000 tonnes and exports of 680,000 tones for the month.

This compared with preliminary exports of 632,441 tonnes in November and 497,841 tonnes in December '95. Total palm oil exports in 1996 are estimated at 7.235 million tonnes, a strong increase of 722,000 tonnes or 11 percent over the previous year. Stocks of PK/PKO were also drawn down sharply by some 35,000 tonnes to around 130,000 tonnes oil basis, because of reduced output and good offtake. Stocks amounted to 152,300 tonnes at end-December 1995. Since our last report of January 7, CPO futures had risen 44-12 ringgit with the spot January contract setting the pace because of nervous shortcovering activities.

For the five-week period to January 10, the January contract had risen 132 ringgit compared to 101 ringgit for February and 79 ringgit for March. The strength in the spot contract is also reflected in the premium (over the March contract) widening from four ringgit at the start of this month to 45 ringgit on January 10. Nearby supplies of physical CPO are likely to become increasingly tight relative to refiners' requirements in the next several weeks. Price advanced further yesterday in response to the limit up gains posted in CBT SB/SBO futures last Friday following the release of bullishly-constructed USDA supply-demand figures for 1996-97.

CPO futures were higher by 48-45 ringgit at the peak before the gains were trimmed to 28-31 ringgit. The January contract settled at 1,345 ringgit and March at 1,300 ringgit. CPO price were at their highest levels in 12 months. Refiners however had to struggle for margins because product prices lagged the gains in the raw material. The unexpected surge in the ringgit against the US dollar, at 2.4690 yesterday - the highest in 17 months, also contributed to the squeeze in refining margins. The USDA pegged the recently harvested US SB crop at 2,382 million bullish, one percent lower than the month ago estimate but 9.4 percent higher than the 1995-96 crop.

Projection on ending stocks at end-August '97 was lowered by 25 million bullish to 155 million bullish. If realised, it would be lower than the previous season's stock of 183 million bullish and the lowest since 1976. U.S SBO stocks at end September this year were projected at 2.015 million lbs, down 125 million LBS from month ago projection and unchanged from the 1995-96 ending stock. CDSBO FOB for March sdhipment was quoted at $528.50 in S. America and $560 in RDM compared to CIF RDM CPO of $572.50.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
